headline: Geometric and index-based measures quantify tumor and omic structure
label: Geometric Frameworks For Biological Data
summary: Recent preprints and a 2026 gastric cancer atlas apply geometric and index-based representations to tumor architecture and omic signatures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the recasting of biological structure as formal geometric objects that can be compared quantitatively, though the items do not all share this. A tile-based index computed from TCGA gastric cancer H&E whole-slide images operationalizes a proposed hyperdisorder regime of multiscale tumor architecture. A separate preprint represents multi-omic signatures as convex polytopes in an 18-dimensional latent space and applies this representation to metabolic data. A spatially resolved gastric cancer atlas integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map a lymphocyte-aggregated region that tracks T cell activation; it provides spatial context in the same tumor type rather than introducing a geometric construct. The methods are heterogeneous, so the shared element is direction rather than a common algorithm. What is new is the distance- or index-based treatment of the biological objects themselves.
